countries.name: United States
countries.overview: The F-1 is a non-immigrant student visa that allows foreign nationals to pursue academic studies at a SEVP-approved US institution. It is one of the most common student visas in the world.

applicationSteps.title: Get Accepted to a SEVP-Approved School
applicationSteps.description: Apply and receive an acceptance letter from a US institution certified by the Student and Exchange Visitor Program (SEVP).

applicationSteps.title: Receive your Form I-20
applicationSteps.description: Your school issues Form I-20 (Certificate of Eligibility). Review all details carefully — name, program dates, and funding must be accurate.

applicationSteps.title: Pay the SEVIS Fee
applicationSteps.description: Pay the $350 SEVIS I-901 fee online at fmjfee.com before scheduling your visa interview. Keep the receipt.

applicationSteps.title: Complete the DS-160 Form
applicationSteps.description: Fill out the Online Nonimmigrant Visa Application (DS-160) on the US Department of State website. Upload a compliant photo.

applicationSteps.title: Schedule Visa Interview
applicationSteps.description: Book an interview appointment at the nearest US Embassy or Consulate. Wait times vary by location and season.
applicationSteps.duration: Days to months depending on location

applicationSteps.title: Attend Visa Interview
applicationSteps.description: Appear at the consulate with all documents. The officer will assess your intent to return home after studies and your financial ability.

applicationSteps.title: Receive Visa & Travel
applicationSteps.description: If approved, your passport is returned with the F-1 visa stamp. You may enter the US up to 30 days before your program start date.

documents: Valid passport (valid for at least 6 months beyond your stay)
Financial evidence (bank statements, sponsor letters, scholarships)
Standardized test scores (SAT, GRE, GMAT if applicable)
Ties to home country (property, family, job offer)
countries.financialRequirement: Must demonstrate sufficient funds to cover tuition + living expenses for the entire program (typically $20,000–$60,000/year depending on institution and location).
tips: Apply for your visa at least 3 months before your program start date.
Consulate officers look for strong ties to your home country to ensure you'll return.
Bring organized originals AND copies of all documents.
Be honest and concise in your interview answers.
F-1 students can work on-campus up to 20 hours/week and may apply for OPT after graduation.
postArrival: Register with your DSO (Designated School Official) within the first week
Get your Social Security Number (SSN) if eligible
Open a US bank account
Understand your visa status maintenance rules

countries.name: United Kingdom
countries.overview: The UK Student Visa (formerly Tier 4) allows international students to study at a UK Higher Education institution with a Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies (CAS) from a licensed sponsor.

applicationSteps.title: Receive University Offer & CAS
applicationSteps.description: Accept your unconditional offer from a UKVI-licensed sponsor institution. They will issue a Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies (CAS) number.

applicationSteps.title: Check Eligibility
applicationSteps.description: Confirm you meet the English language requirement (B2 CEFR), financial requirements, and that your course is at RQF Level 6 or above for degree programs.

applicationSteps.title: Apply Online
applicationSteps.description: Submit your Student Visa application on the UK Visas and Immigration (UKVI) portal. You can apply up to 6 months before your course start date.

applicationSteps.title: Pay Visa Fee & Immigration Health Surcharge
applicationSteps.description: Pay the £363 visa fee and the Immigration Health Surcharge (IHS) — currently £776/year, giving access to NHS services.

applicationSteps.title: Book Biometrics Appointment
applicationSteps.description: Attend a Visa Application Centre (VAC) to provide fingerprints and a photo. Some countries allow document upload instead.

applicationSteps.title: Submit Documents
applicationSteps.description: Upload supporting documents online or submit in person at the VAC. Await a decision.

applicationSteps.title: Collect BRP & Travel
applicationSteps.description: If approved, travel to the UK within the vignette dates. Collect your Biometric Residence Permit (BRP) within 10 days of arrival.

documents: Bank statements showing required funds (28 consecutive days)
English language test results (IELTS, TOEFL, etc.)
ATAS certificate (if your subject requires it)
TB test results (if from a listed country)
countries.financialRequirement: £1,334/month for courses in London, £1,023/month outside London. Must be held for 28 consecutive days before application.
tips: Apply as early as possible — up to 6 months before your course.
Ensure your 28-day bank statement window is timed correctly.
The IHS fee is substantial — budget for it separately.
ATAS clearance can take 20+ working days — apply early if needed.
You can work up to 20 hours/week during term time.
postArrival: Collect your BRP from the designated Post Office within 10 days
Register with a GP (doctor) for NHS access
Open a UK bank account (many require proof of address)
Register with your university's international student office

countries.name: Australia
countries.overview: The Student Visa (Subclass 500) allows international students to study a full-time registered course in Australia. It replaced the previous student visa subclasses in 2016.

applicationSteps.title: Enroll in a CRICOS-Registered Course
applicationSteps.description: Apply and gain acceptance into a course registered on the Commonwealth Register of Institutions and Courses for Overseas Students (CRICOS).

applicationSteps.title: Receive Confirmation of Enrolment (CoE)
applicationSteps.description: Once you pay your initial tuition fees, your institution issues a CoE — a unique code required for your visa application.

applicationSteps.title: Obtain Overseas Student Health Cover (OSHC)
applicationSteps.description: Purchase OSHC for the full duration of your visa. This is mandatory and must be arranged before applying.

applicationSteps.title: Create ImmiAccount & Apply Online
applicationSteps.description: Create an ImmiAccount on the Department of Home Affairs website and submit your Subclass 500 visa application.

applicationSteps.title: Provide Biometrics (if required)
applicationSteps.description: Some nationalities must provide biometrics at a Visa Application Centre. Check if your country requires this.

applicationSteps.title: Health Examination
applicationSteps.description: Complete an Australian immigration medical exam through an approved panel physician if requested.

applicationSteps.title: Await Decision & Travel
applicationSteps.description: The visa grant is sent electronically to your ImmiAccount. There is no visa stamp — your passport number is linked to the visa.

countries.financialRequirement: Must demonstrate funds for: first year tuition + AUD $21,041 (living costs) + AUD $7,362 per accompanying spouse + AUD $3,152 per child.
tips: The GTE statement is crucial — explain why you want to study in Australia and why you'll return home.
Apply at least 2–3 months before your intended travel date.
Australia's visa is electronically linked; you won't get a physical stamp.
Students can work up to 48 hours per fortnight during semester.
Health insurance (OSHC) can often be arranged through your university at group rates.
postArrival: Get your Tax File Number (TFN) to work legally
Open an Australian bank account
Enroll in your university orientation program
Familiarize yourself with OSHC and how to use it

countries.name: Canada
countries.overview: Canada offers two pathways: the Student Direct Stream (SDS) for faster processing from select countries, and the regular study permit route. A study permit is required for courses longer than 6 months.

applicationSteps.title: Receive Acceptance Letter (LOA)
applicationSteps.description: Get accepted to a Designated Learning Institution (DLI) in Canada. The Letter of Acceptance is a mandatory document.

applicationSteps.title: Choose SDS or Regular Stream
applicationSteps.description: SDS is available to students from India, China, Philippines, Vietnam, and other listed countries with IELTS 6.0+ and upfront GIC payment. Others use the regular stream.

applicationSteps.title: Get a Guaranteed Investment Certificate (GIC)
applicationSteps.description: For SDS, purchase a GIC of CAD $10,000 from a participating Canadian bank. This proves financial readiness.

applicationSteps.title: Apply Online via IRCC Portal
applicationSteps.description: Create a MyCIC account and submit your study permit application with all required documents.

applicationSteps.title: Provide Biometrics
applicationSteps.description: After application, you'll receive a Biometric Instruction Letter. Visit a VAC within 30 days to provide fingerprints and photo.

applicationSteps.title: Medical Exam (if required)
applicationSteps.description: Some nationalities must complete an upfront medical exam through a Panel Physician. Check IRCC guidelines.

applicationSteps.title: Receive PAL / ePAL & Travel
applicationSteps.description: If approved, you receive a Port of Entry Letter of Introduction (PAL). Your actual study permit is issued at the Canadian border.

documents: Letter of Acceptance from a DLI
Proof of financial support (GIC + tuition proof for SDS)
countries.financialRequirement: Must show: first year tuition + CAD $10,000 (GIC for SDS) or equivalent living funds for regular stream. Additional funds required for family members.
tips: SDS significantly reduces wait times — use it if your country is eligible.
A strong Statement of Purpose explaining your career goals in Canada is essential.
Canada allows students to work off-campus up to 20 hours/week.
Post-Graduation Work Permit (PGWP) allows up to 3 years of work after graduation.
French language skills can strengthen your application for Quebec institutions.
postArrival: Get your Social Insurance Number (SIN) for working
Open a Canadian bank account and access your GIC funds
Register with provincial health insurance
Attend international student orientation at your institution

countries.name: Germany
countries.overview: Germany offers tuition-free education at public universities for both EU and non-EU students. A national (Type D) student visa is required for non-EU nationals planning to study for more than 90 days.
countries.validity: Usually issued for 3 months to obtain residence permit in Germany

applicationSteps.title: Apply & Get University Admission
applicationSteps.description: Apply to a German university (staatliche Universität). Most public universities charge no tuition. Get your official admission letter (Zulassungsbescheid).

applicationSteps.title: Open Blocked Account (Sperrkonto)
applicationSteps.description: Open a German blocked account with a minimum of €11,208 (2024 requirement). Providers include Fintiba, Expatrio, Deutsche Bank. Funds are released monthly after arrival.

applicationSteps.title: Get Health Insurance
applicationSteps.description: Obtain German statutory health insurance (gesetzliche Krankenversicherung) or recognized private health insurance. TK, AOK, and Barmer are common providers.

applicationSteps.title: Book Visa Appointment at German Embassy
applicationSteps.description: Schedule an appointment at the German embassy or consulate in your home country. Slots fill up quickly — book months in advance.

applicationSteps.title: Prepare & Submit Documents
applicationSteps.description: Submit all required documents at your appointment. Documents in languages other than German/English must be officially translated.

applicationSteps.title: Await Visa Decision
applicationSteps.description: The consulate processes your application. You may be asked for additional documents.

applicationSteps.title: Travel & Register (Anmeldung)
applicationSteps.description: Travel to Germany. Within 2 weeks of arrival, register your address at the local Bürgeramt (Anmeldung). Then apply for a residence permit at the Ausländerbehörde.

documents: Academic transcripts and diplomas (certified translations if needed)
German language proof (if program is in German — TestDaF, DSH)
English language proof (for English-taught programs — IELTS/TOEFL)
APS certificate (mandatory for students from China, India, Vietnam, Mongolia)
countries.financialRequirement: Must deposit €11,208 into a German blocked account (Sperrkonto). This covers approximately €934/month for 12 months of living expenses.
tips: Book your embassy appointment as soon as you receive your admission letter — slots fill up fast.
APS certificate is mandatory for Indian, Chinese, and Vietnamese applicants — this process takes 4–8 weeks alone.
Public universities charge minimal semester fees (€150–€350) but no tuition.
Learn basic German — even in English programs, daily life requires it.
The blocked account is released in monthly installments once you're in Germany.
postArrival: Complete Anmeldung (address registration) within 2 weeks
Apply for residence permit at Ausländerbehörde
Enroll in health insurance if not already active
Open a German bank account (Girokonto)
Get a German SIM card and set up university student portal

countries.name: Japan
countries.overview: Japan's student visa (留学ビザ) is issued for enrollment in Japanese universities, language schools, or vocational colleges. Japan's education system is highly regarded, and the visa process is managed through the institution.

applicationSteps.title: Apply to a Japanese Institution
applicationSteps.description: Apply to a MEXT-recognized university, Japanese language school, or vocational school. Receive your admission letter.

applicationSteps.title: Institution Applies for Certificate of Eligibility (CoE)
applicationSteps.description: Your school applies to the regional Immigration Bureau on your behalf for a Certificate of Eligibility (在留資格認定証明書). This is the central document.

applicationSteps.title: Receive CoE & Apply for Visa
applicationSteps.description: Once your school sends you the CoE, take it to the Japanese Embassy/Consulate in your country along with other documents to apply for the student visa.

applicationSteps.title: Submit Visa Application
applicationSteps.description: Submit your visa application form, CoE, passport, photos, and other required documents at the Japanese consulate.

applicationSteps.title: Receive Visa & Travel
applicationSteps.description: Collect your passport with the student visa sticker. Travel to Japan before the CoE expiry date (within 3 months of issuance).

applicationSteps.title: Residence Card at Airport
applicationSteps.description: Upon arrival at major airports (Narita, Haneda, Kansai), receive your Residence Card (在留カード). Register your address at the local city hall within 14 days.

documents: Certificate of Eligibility (CoE) — issued by your school
Visa application form (from Japanese consulate website)
countries.financialRequirement: Must show sufficient funds: approximately ¥1,500,000–¥2,000,000 per year (tuition + living expenses). Language schools may require advance tuition payment.
tips: The CoE application is handled by your institution — follow their specific guidance closely.
Apply to JASSO (Japan Student Services Organization) scholarships to reduce financial burden.
MEXT government scholarships are highly competitive but cover full tuition and stipend.
Students can work up to 28 hours/week with a part-time work permit.
Learn basic Japanese before arriving — it makes daily life significantly easier.
postArrival: Register your address at City Hall (市役所) within 14 days
Obtain your My Number (社会保障・税番号) card
Enroll in the National Health Insurance (国民健康保険)
Open a Japanese bank account (Japan Post Bank is easiest for newcomers)
Get a part-time work permit from your school if you plan to work

countries.name: New Zealand
countries.overview: New Zealand's student visa allows international students to study at a New Zealand Qualifications Authority (NZQA)-approved institution. The country is known for its welcoming environment and high quality of life.

applicationSteps.title: Enroll in an NZQA-Approved Institution
applicationSteps.description: Apply and receive an offer of place from a New Zealand university, polytechnic, or private training establishment registered with NZQA.

applicationSteps.title: Purchase Acceptable Travel & Medical Insurance
applicationSteps.description: Obtain comprehensive health and travel insurance for the duration of your study. Some universities offer group policies.

applicationSteps.title: Apply Online via Immigration NZ
applicationSteps.description: Submit your student visa application through Immigration New Zealand's online portal (RealMe login required).

applicationSteps.title: Provide Biometrics (if required)
applicationSteps.description: Certain nationalities must provide biometric information. Check INZ guidelines.

applicationSteps.title: Medical & Character Checks
applicationSteps.description: Undergo a medical examination by an INZ-approved physician and obtain police clearance certificates.

applicationSteps.title: Await Decision & Travel
applicationSteps.description: Receive visa decision. Your visa label is placed in your passport. Travel to New Zealand before the visa start date.

documents: Offer of place from an approved New Zealand institution
Return travel booking or funds for return travel
Police clearance (if 17+ and lived abroad for 12+ months)
countries.financialRequirement: NZD $15,000 per year for living expenses, plus tuition fees already paid. Must show sufficient funds through bank statements or a financial sponsor.
tips: New Zealand is one of the easier countries to get a student visa for — maintain clean financials.
Students can work 20 hours/week during study and full-time during scheduled holidays.
Post-Study Work Visa available for up to 3 years after graduation.
New Zealand's points-based immigration system offers a clear pathway to PR.
Healthcare is partially covered for longer-term students through accident compensation.
postArrival: Enroll in your institution and confirm studies have commenced
Get an IRD (tax) number for working
Open a New Zealand bank account
Register with a local GP for health services

countries.name: South Korea
countries.overview: The D-2 visa is for foreign students attending degree programs at Korean universities or colleges. South Korea is increasingly popular due to its world-class universities, K-culture, and post-graduation opportunities.

applicationSteps.title: Get Accepted to a Korean University
applicationSteps.description: Apply and receive an official admission letter from a recognized Korean university. Top institutions include Seoul National University, Yonsei, KAIST, and POSTECH.

applicationSteps.title: Prepare Required Documents
applicationSteps.description: Gather all documents including admission letter, financial proof, academic records, and health certificate. Documents must often be apostilled or notarized.

applicationSteps.title: Apply at Korean Embassy or Consulate
applicationSteps.description: Visit the Korean embassy or consulate in your country. Submit the application form with all required documents in person.

applicationSteps.title: Await Visa Decision
applicationSteps.description: Processing takes 2–4 weeks. You may be called for an interview in some cases.

applicationSteps.title: Collect Visa & Travel
applicationSteps.description: Collect your passport with D-2 visa stamp. Travel to South Korea and enter before the visa validity starts.

applicationSteps.title: Register as Alien (ARC)
applicationSteps.description: Within 90 days of arrival, register at the local Immigration Office to get your Alien Registration Card (ARC). This is your ID in Korea.

documents: Official admission letter from Korean university
Financial proof: minimum ₩10,000,000 (~$7,500 USD) in bank account
Korean language proficiency (TOPIK) if program is in Korean
Certificate of family relationship (if sponsored by family)
countries.financialRequirement: Must demonstrate at least ₩10,000,000 (~USD $7,500) in personal or sponsor funds. Some universities require proof of tuition payment in advance.
tips: Learning basic Korean (Hangul) before arrival will greatly improve daily life quality.
TOPIK (Test of Proficiency in Korean) Level 3+ is typically required for Korean-medium programs.
Government of Korea (GKS) scholarships are fully funded — apply through your country's Korean embassy.
D-2 visa holders can work part-time up to 20 hours/week with a work permit from immigration.
The ARC card is required to open a bank account and get a phone plan — get it as soon as possible.
postArrival: Register for Alien Registration Card (ARC) at local immigration office
Open a Korean bank account (KEB Hana, Shinhan, or KB Kookmin are popular)
Get a Korean phone number (telecom shops require ARC)
Register at your university and attend orientation
Apply for part-time work permit at immigration if you plan to work
